title: Lorenzo Tio at the Pekin: lazy clarinetist and the High Society variation
summary: Howard worked with Manuel Perez's band at the Pekin with Tio, who played while turning a newspaper page, and learned High Society from him.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Well, I'll tell you one thing, before I even thought about a clarinet, I used to- Oh, I got to tell you I worked with Manu Perez too. You did work for- Yeah, Teal was in that band at the Pekin. Who was in that band?
Yeah, that was my favorite. You weren't playing violin, you were playing clarinet?

Yeah. You know that's how Barney plays sometimes? Yes. They got music supposedly. Barney got a newspaper on the thing, you know. Well Teal was just the opposite. He's six foot something, you know. His leg crossed, he was the laziest clarinet player I've ever seen in my life. He was playing and they got a newspaper and he stopped playing to turn the page.
Wonderful clarinet player. But I hear he was one of the greatest of all.

Yes sir. He taught Barney, Simeon, Fazola, oh yeah. But how about you? What about me? Did he teach you? No. No. In 1937, first time I'd seen him in New York, he said, how long have you been playing clarinet? Oh yeah? I said, oh I don't know. He said, well you played the hell out of it, Father, I'm concerned. That's what he told me. It made me feel wonderful. Did he die in New York?

Yeah. What did clarinet play? The high society I play now, I learn on the fiddle. Oh really? Yeah, because I played it, just the variation, he wrote it down. I'll never forget he wrote it for clarinet and I had to transpose it to E flat, see. And the very same high society is what I play on there, is what he wrote down. It's a little different from when they play it.
A little different. I asked him one time, I said, you take all of, where do you take your breath? Because when I'm playing a thing like this, there ain't no place to take no breath. Yes.
Okay. I played a melody, he played a, we first played a duet, see. And then I would play the variation and he played in Lowell Raster.
